summary: Compare source numerics by Decimal value, clarify calculation evidence rules and retain granular safe validator diagnostics for Reference QA.
decision_refs: C5 failed because the source used $2000.00 while the model emitted 2,000; string comparison rejected an identical numeric value.
Calculation operands may occupy several exact evidence rows, while layout_lines remains navigation context and never becomes citation support.
A controlled Pro sequence produced fully usable C1 and C5 answers and a partial C3 answer; the corresponding Flash smoke remained unstable, so another full Flash run was not justified.
A same-page numeric citation-closure prototype showed zero live completions and did not prevent an incorrect C1 answer; it was rolled back.
Historical verification note: Decimal-equivalent source operand and claim-number validation
Historical verification note: prompt and safe diagnostic category regressions
Historical verification note: controlled Pro and Flash C1/C3/C5 smoke evaluations with explicit human adjudication
Historical verification note: negative same-page closure experiment rolled back after audit
Historical verification note: full Python, localization, spec, change and bundle gates
approval_evidence: The user explicitly allowed API calls and directed CIRP development, testing and iteration to continue.
known_limitations: Numeric equivalence fixes representation-only rejection; it does not identify missing disciplines, repair OCR/layout ambiguity or make a wrong operand semantically correct.
Flash remained unstable on C1/C3/C5 and generated one contract-valid but incorrect C1 answer in a later diagnostic smoke.
The final DEV-168 prompt and code have not been rerun as a complete fixed-15 Flash/Pro pair, so the DEV-167 baseline remains the latest fair full comparison.
